title: Atomic-Scale Investigation of Cation Intercalation in 1D Lepidocrocite Titanate Nanofilaments via STEM-EELS
content: Titanate nanostructures are typically produced through hydrothermal and sol-gel synthesis, but these methods often result in larger structures due to crystal growth at high temperatures. Badr et al. [1] developed an alternative approach to address this challenge, synthesizing 1D titania-based nanofilaments (NFs) from earth-abundant, Ti-containing, and non-toxic precursors. These lepidocrocite titanates possess exceptional ion exchange capabilities, making them particularly well-suited for cation intercalation studies. Based on atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), electron diffraction patterns, and density functional theory (DFT) modeling, we observed that the TiO2 nanofilaments (NFs) predominantly grow along the [200] direction while stacking along the b-axis within self-assembled bundles or larger 2D flakes. Cross-sectional views of aligned TiO2 nanoribbons reveal a lepidocrocite-based structure with minimal cross-sectional dimensions of 5 × 7 Å2[2,3].
